summary: OpenAI announced an expansion of its Daybreak cybersecurity effort, including an updated Codex Security plugin, the full release of GPT-5.5-Cyber to trusted defenders, a Daybreak Cyber Partner Program, and the Patch the Planet open-source vulnerability remediation initiative.

mechanisms.reason: OpenAI describes Codex Security as an agent that performs security-engineer tasks end-to-end (discovery, validation, patching) in place of human review, and states it operates at scale across tens of thousands of codebases.
mechanisms.quote: We built Codex Security around a simple premise: put the equivalent of a security engineer next to every software developer by integrating directly into Codex.

mechanisms.reason: The document discloses large-scale usage figures for an agentic scanning/patching product, indicating substantial and growing inference volume from this workflow.
mechanisms.quote: Since launching Codex Security cloud in research preview in March, it has scanned over 30 million commits across more than 30,000 codebases; human reviewers have manually marked more than 70,000 findings as fixed, and over 500,000 findings have automatically been determined to be fixed.

practices.reason: GPT-5.5-Cyber is an updated, more capable and permissive model for vulnerability discovery and patch generation with stated benchmark gains, but access is restricted to verified defenders so broad adoption isn't yet possible.
practices.quote: On CyberGym, which measures whether an agent can reproduce known vulnerabilities in software environments, the updated GPT‑5.5‑Cyber reached 85.6% in single-model evaluations, compared with 81.8% for GPT‑5.5.

practices.reason: The document names and quantifies performance on named security benchmarks (CyberGym, ExploitGym, SEC-bench Pro), giving a concrete measurement bar a security engineering team could adopt for evaluating models.
practices.quote: GPT‑5.5‑Cyber also outperformed GPT‑5.5 on two demanding real-world security benchmarks: 39.5% versus 25.95% on ExploitGym, which tests whether agents can turn known vulnerabilities into working exploits that achieve unauthorized code execution.

practices.reason: The plugin describes a concrete pipeline for going from code scan to validated patch (threat modeling, reachability analysis, evidence gathering, patch generation, verification) that a team could model their own security automation on.
practices.quote: Rather than just generating alerts, Codex Security will understand your team’s code and its threat model (or generate one if it doesn’t exist), identify plausible vulnerabilities, determine whether affected code is reachable, gather evidence to provide validation steps, develop a targeted patch, and verify the result.

practices.reason: The updated plugin adds new export/integration surfaces (SARIF, CodeQL, vulnerability management systems) that a team running Codex would need to wire into existing security tooling.
practices.quote: When Codex Security completes a scan, it can also export to an existing vulnerability management system or integrate into tools with SARIF files, CodeQL queries, and more.
